--- title: "Final syllable deletion" subtitle: "Automatically generated task sheet · CF_SUPRESION_SILABA_FINAL" --- ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} **Automatically generated task sheet** (A · Accuracy; quality class A). Generated on November 27, 2026 with `scripts/R/ficha_generica_v3.R --tarea CF_SUPRESION_SILABA_FINAL`. Figures come from the data; the theoretical framework is shared by the tasks of the same construct. **Interpretation and team review are missing.** Spanish name: *Supresión de la sílaba final*. [Spanish version](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/auto/CF_SUPRESION_SILABA_FINAL.html). ::: **In one sentence.** Final syllable deletion, at age 4 (1,338 administrations in 3 cohorts). AUC .51–.63 against persistent reading difficulty. ## Description | | | |---|---| | Codes | 1834 | | Battery | LEEDUCA | | Format | pictures on screen | | Items | 10 (1834) according to the platform | | Task family | A · Accuracy | | Score | Correct responses | | Instructions (platform) | The child was instructed to delete a speech sound and to provide the remaining word or pseudoword. Correct responses, errors and time were recorded. | ## How it is programmed on the platform The platform is the reference: what the activity actually presents is what is measured. Configuration read from the activity itself on 23/10/2026 (without modifying it). Cell contents are in Spanish. | Code|Name on the platform |Presentation | Test items| Practice items|Example items |Time limit |Order |Scoring | Age.term (label 3)| |----:|:----------------------|:----------------------|----------:|--------------:|:-------------|:----------|:-----|:--------|------------------:| | 1834|Supresión sílaba final |Un dibujo por pantalla | 10| 1|— |— |fijo |Aciertos | 4, 4.3, 5| **Differences from the dictionary or the instructions (in Spanish):** - **1834.** 1 de entrenamiento + 10 de prueba. *Age.term: provisional reading of the activity's label 3 (3rd digit = age, 4th = term; 0 = annual), to be confirmed with the engineer.* **How it looks on the platform** (first item or example; 2026 screenshot; the interface is in Spanish). ::: {layout-ncol=1} ![1834 · Supresión sílaba final](../../figuras/plataforma/1834.jpg){.lightbox width="40%" fig-alt="Screenshot of activity 1834"} ::: ## Theoretical framework Phonological awareness is the ability to reflect on and manipulate the sounds of speech. The platform's tasks cover a continuum of difficulty: - by **unit**: syllable or phoneme; - by **operation**: counting, identifying, segmenting or deleting; - by **position**: initial, final or any. The "all positions" version mixes items and is the most demanding. **What the evidence says:** - **Phonemes and manipulation are what most distinguish dyslexia.** In 2,252 children from six European languages, phoneme deletion and RAN were the strongest concurrent predictors of dyslexia [@landerl2013predictors]. In consistent orthographies, children with dyslexia perform below even younger readers of the same reading level on phoneme manipulation tasks, but not on syllable tasks [@parrila2020rlmatch]. - **In Spanish, phonological awareness develops in stages**, from the syllable to the phoneme. Phonemic awareness builds on learning to read and at the same time drives it: the relation is reciprocal [@denton2000pa]. Phonological awareness predicts above all the reading of complex syllables [@martinez2020silabica]. - **Its predictive value is universal, but changes with age.** Phonemic awareness, letters and RAN predict reading growth equally in Spanish, Czech and English [@caravolas2013growth]. Its relation with fluency, however, is more complex and depends on task and age, whereas RAN predicts fluency in all languages [@landerl2019pa]. This is what @catts2026definicion lead us to expect: precursors are useful for early prognosis and lose weight once there is reading to measure. The pilot task sheets develop this framework in more detail: [syllable counting](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/CF523.html) and [rapid naming](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/RAN.html) (*in Spanish*). **What our data show.** The pattern matches the literature: - **What predicts best.** Deletion tasks in all positions are those that best predict low Woodcock-Muñoz fluency (median AUC .72–.73, up to .81). - **In between.** The other deletion and identification tasks (.63–.68). - **What predicts least.** Phoneme segmentation and syllable counting (.60–.62). - **Consistency and stability.** Internal consistency is good (α = .82–.94), but stability between terms is low (ρ = .27–.41). Many tasks were given in only one or two sessions, and children change quickly at these ages. For an individual decision, the result should be confirmed at two time points. ## Sample and descriptive statistics | Time point| Cohort| Session|School year | N| Non-Preleo| Preleo| Schools| |----------:|------:|-------:|:-----------|---:|----------:|------:|-------:| | 4.2| 2012| 157|2016/17 | 337| 334| 0| 17| | 4.3| 2011| 141|2015/16 | 577| 0| 577| 32| | 4.3| 2013| 191|2017/18 | 424| 414| 10| 23| | Time point| N| Cohorts| Mean| SD| Median| Skewness| % floor| % ceiling| |----------:|---:|-------:|----:|----:|------:|--------:|-------:|---------:| | 4.2| 334| 2012| 4.25| 3.80| 3| 0.30| 19.16| 12.57| | 4.3| 414| 2013| 4.43| 3.86| 3| 0.28| 20.05| 15.94| **Score range** (non-Preleo group, in correct responses). The usual range goes from P1 to P99 (98% of the children). The minimum–maximum is the one observed after cleaning; the possible range is 0–10 correct responses. | Time point| N|Usual range (P1–P99) |Min.–max. |Possible range | Warning| |----------:|---:|:--------------------|:---------|:--------------|-------:| | 4.2| 334|0–10 |0–10 |0–10 | | | 4.3| 414|0–10 |0–10 |0–10 | | ## Reliability There are no two time points with the same children (at least 80). α (2021) = .93. ## Validity **Concurrent.** With other tasks in its own domain (Phonological awareness), r = .26. Outside its domain, the highest relation is with: Vocabulary and oral comprehension (4.2, r = .28); Letter knowledge (4.3, r = .20). **Against reading difficulty and comprehension.** Against persistent difficulty, AUC .51–.63. Against poor comprehension one or two school years later (non-circular criterion), AUC .60. ![Validity: AUC with 95% confidence interval (labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_CF_SUPRESION_SILABA_FINAL_F2_validez.png){width=85%} **Against an external criterion, years later.** Against low Woodcock-Muñoz reading fluency in 2021/22 ([chapter](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/criterio-woodcock.html), *in Spanish*), AUC .57 (1 time point; 344–344 children). ## Provisional norms | Time point| N| Cohorts| P5| P10| P16| P25| P50| P75| P90| |----------:|---:|-------:|--:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 4.2| 334| 2012| 0| 0| 0| 1| 3| 8| 10| | 4.3| 414| 2013| 0| 0| 0| 1| 3| 9| 10| **Floor effect.** At 4.2 and 4.3 P10 coincides with the worst possible score: many children are tied at the minimum and the norms do not distinguish between them. At those time points this task cannot be used to grade difficulty. These are norms by time point (school year × term). For dates between assessments and time points without a normative sample, study M3 proposes continuous norms on **months of instruction**, not on age, with relative age within the school year as an adjustment. ![Provisional norms (non-Preleo schools; labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_CF_SUPRESION_SILABA_FINAL_F1_baremo.png){width=85%} ## Variables that affect it |Variable | Time point| n| Effect| p| |:---------------------------------------|----------:|-----:|------:|-----:| |School SES (ρ) | 4.2| 233| 0.000| 1.000| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 4.2| 337| -0.009| 0.934| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 4.2| 334| 0.194| 0.000| |School (ICC) | 4.2| 337| 0.167| | |School SES (ρ) | 4.3| 1,001| 0.134| 0.000| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 4.3| 979| 0.048| 0.452| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 4.3| 976| 0.152| 0.000| |School (ICC) | 4.3| 1,001| 0.231| | ## For publications The LEEDUCA platform task “Final syllable deletion” (code 1834; LEEDUCA battery) assesses syllable awareness (final syllable deletion). Each item is presented with a picture on the screen; the examiner gives the instruction orally and records the child's response. It comprises 10 items. The time limit is 120 seconds. It is administered individually on a computer at school. In the 2011, 2012 and 2013 cohorts it was administered in 3 sessions, from 4 years of age. The main outcome is the number of correct responses. In our data (2021 analyses), internal consistency was α = .93 (N = 976, 10 items). Against later poor reading comprehension, AUC = .60. ## Pending issues - Ceiling effect at 4.3 (more than 15% of children with the maximum score). - Floor effect at 4.2, 4.3 (more than 15% with zero correct). - Floor effect in the norms at 4.2 and 4.3: at least 10% of children have the worst possible score, so P10 does not exist. At those time points the "severe" and "very severe" levels must not be assigned with this task (study M3). - La puntuación máxima observada (11) supera el número de ítems (10): puede que se puntúen los ítems de ejemplo, que haya una versión con más ítems o un error de datos. Comprobar antes de describir la tarea y distinguir ítems de prueba y de ejemplo. *(Spanish)* - **Dictionary correction.** Corregida el 2026-10-21: antes F_EJEC_MEM_OP_MEMORIA_CONCEPTOS. La consigna de la plataforma, el Organizador 9.1 («CF - Supresión de sílabas PF») y la ficha de la tesis de María describen la supresión de la sílaba final (ejemplo: patada → pata). La etiqueta «Memoria Conceptos» de las matrices antiguas era errónea. *(Spanish)* - Write the interpretation; review with the team.
